messages.author: 97ce067823027f53
messages.subject: Statistics/Psychology Question in R
parts:
Hey all, a question arose in a psychological experiment. We measure
anxiety, working memory (WM), and analogical performance. A theory
says that anxiety exerts its effect on analogical performance
(changing analogies from relational/abstract to more attributial/
surface-based) only by reducing WM. We can compute best-fit functions
with lm between anxiety->WM, WM->analogy, and anxiety->analogy.
Composing the first two functions, we can proceed from anxiety scores
to their predicted WM scores to analogical performance. Now we want to
test if this composition function is "signficantly similar" to the
observed best-fit lm function from anxiety->analogy. Any clue on how
to do that statistically and implement in R? All variables are
interval/ratio.

I am not sure this question wouldn't be better (and with more promise
of good responses) asked in the Stats for Linguistics newsgroup, given
that the q doesn't involve corpus data, but here's a first shot at an
answer: how about computing partial correlations (e.g.,
<http://www.yilab.gatech.edu/pcor.html>)?

in social psychological research: Conceptual, strategic, and statistical
considerations. Journal of Personality & Social Psychology, 51(6), 1173-1182.
